    [c2] NULL: annotator pool does not change the leaderboard; item-level divergence does not aggregate
    
    Problem: test whether choosing expert vs crowd gold labels changes model ranking -
    the analysis arXiv 2410.19133 explicitly leaves as future work in its Limitations.
    
    Evidence: runs/c2/eval.json, zero GPU, pure re-analysis of existing labels.
    NULL on the headline: expert-gold and crowd-gold leaderboards are IDENTICAL,
    Kendall tau=1.0000, 95% CI [0.8667, 1.0000] over 2000 paired bootstrap resamples,
    0/6 models displaced. Reported as a null per the pre-registered bar rather than
    enlarging the model set to hunt for a flip.
    What survives: 16.8% of items (1,755/10,461) have expert and crowd majorities
    choosing OPPOSITE winners with ties excluded; 49.8% differ in majority label
    overall; divergence is flat across model-quality gaps (48.1% close vs 51.9% wide).
    Also recorded as NOT REAL: the soft-vs-hard tau=0.8667 is one adjacent swap
    between models 0.5pp apart - statistically indistinguishable, must not be claimed.
    Limitation recorded: 6 widely-spaced models is a weak test of rank stability.
    
    Next: C3, which annotator pool do LLM judges track - now the highest-value
    remaining experiment and the only one needing GPU.

h1_ranking_milestones.title: C2/H1: does whose-gold or soft-vs-hard change the leaderboard?
h1_ranking_milestones.notes: PRE-REGISTERED KILL: Kendall tau > 0.9 between disagreement-aware and single-label rankings across all team configurations - report the null and stop. Baselines a reviewer will demand: majority vote, Dawid-Skene, and STABLEVAL (2605.02122) itself. Five team configs: agent-only, human-only, agent-proposes/human-reviews, human-proposes/agent-reviews, agent-with-abstention+escalation. RESULT: NULL. tau=1.0000, CI [0.8667,1.0000], 0/6 displaced. Pre-registered bar said report the null and stop, not enlarge the sweep. Complied.
